summary: A short BBN note correcting and supplementing RFC 442 on IMP flow control. It points to two formal BBN publications as better sources and warns that the host-to-IMP interface had recently changed in ways that matter to people writing network control programs. It updates RFC 442.

eli5.summary: Someone read another person's explanation of the traffic rules, said it was mostly fine, and pointed to the official books for the exact details.

subtitle: A short BBN note saying RFC 442 on IMP flow control is mostly accurate but points to better official sources.

tldr.problem: RFC 442 described IMPSYS flow control from a March 1972 meeting, but it did not cite BBN's two formal publications on the subject.
tldr.mechanism: Dave Walden says the notes are reasonably accurate, then lists the two publications that should be read instead and stresses one for NCP programmers.
tldr.outcome: It is a pointer and correction note that updates RFC 442, not a protocol specification.

today: RFC 449 has no recorded status and updates RFC 442. It is a short pointer note rather than a specification.

sections.title: A Correction to RFC 442
sections.content:
RFC 449, by Dave Walden of BBN, comments on RFC 442, Vint's notes on IMPSYS flow control from the March 16, 1972 meeting. Walden says those notes are reasonably accurate and that they do cite BBN's Quarterly Technical Report #13.

He adds that he might have done better to cite BBN's two formal publications on the flow-control scheme.
sections.eli5: The note says the earlier write-up was fine, but there are better official books to read.

sections.title: The Two Publications
sections.content:
The two recommended sources are a paper by McQuillan et al., Improvements in the Design and Performance of the ARPA Network, in the AFIPS 1972 FJCC proceedings (pp. 741-754), and BBN Report 1822, Specifications for the Interconnection of a Host and an IMP, December 1972 Revision, section 3 (pp. 17-35).

The note calls the second one particularly important reading for NCP programmers, because things have recently changed somewhat.
sections.eli5: Two official documents are named. The second one matters most for people writing the programs that talk to the network, because the rules changed a little.

sections.title: The Inter-IMP Acknowledgement
sections.content:
The inter-IMP acknowledgement mechanism, described in the last section of RFC 442, is also described in the first publication. An almost identical mechanism appears in Appendix F of BBN Report 1822.

The note says this acknowledgement is of only intellectual interest to most Hosts, since it is transparent to network users. The description in Report 1822 is, however, of vital interest to so-called Very Distant Hosts.
sections.eli5: Most computers never see the behind-the-scenes receipts between network boxes. A few far-away ones need to know about them.
